long_biography.plain_text:
Dotty's grew from Craig Estey's observation that traditional bars did not serve older women and couples comfortably. After becoming a video-poker distributor, he visited gaming venues across several western states and designed a cleaner, friendlier tavern around that audience. He bought six Nevada locations in 1995 and refined the format for several years before the original stores became profitable.

Estey coupled that customer focus with tight operational control. Nevada Restaurant Services distributes supplies, repairs and tests machines, and has manufactured some equipment used by the chain. He remains sole owner of the company's active gaming locations, with separate executives holding finance, operations and general-management roles.

uncertainties.detail: Official records use Richard Craig Estey, while testimony and business reporting usually use Craig Estey. The biography preserves the full legal-style name and identifies Craig as the working name; no source-field name correction is needed.

The current gaming register directly lists Estey at 100 percent ownership, not merely as a director. Other company information names separate current executives, so the dossier does not infer beneficial ownership from a board or officer role and does not depend on an unverified trust relationship.

The existing source gives July 1953 but no day. The dedicated Wikipedia page has no birth date and inconsistently displays Oregon while categorising the place of birth as missing. Oregon is therefore retained only as a sub-threshold candidate, and no birth-day proposal is made.

A family vending and food-distribution business is reported, but the sources reviewed do not establish whether it supplied Dotty's launch capital or another material advantage. The broad Self-made origin is used rather than an independent or advantaged subtype.

Gaming records carry president, secretary, treasurer and director roles, while other current company information identifies separate executive leadership. The proposed known-for title uses the durable founder and sole-owner roles rather than a potentially changing corporate title.

The existing Wikipedia page matches the exact identity. No personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website was verified; a LinkedIn result for a Massachusetts technology professional is a namesake and was rejected. The Dotty's domain was identified but was not proposed as a personal profile.
The public business record is strong but the personal biographical record remains sparse. Private-family trivia, allegations, controversies, legal disputes and vessel-specific research were excluded.
